prompt: Match each part of Airflow to its job.

pairs.right: Reads the DAG files and stores each DAG
Decides which runs and tasks are due
Waits on behalf of waiting tasks
Holds every run and every task's state

right_distractors: Transforms the rows the tasks read

prompt: A colleague's task reads a million orders into a Python list, sorts them, and returns the list to the next task. What is wrong with that, in Airflow?

choices.text: Nothing; that is what tasks are for
choices.why: Tasks run work; the data belongs in the warehouse, not in Airflow.

choices.text: Python lists cannot hold a million items
choices.why: They can; the problem is where the list ends up.

choices.text: Airflow is not a data engine
choices.why: Right. The rows go into Airflow's own database; the sort belongs in SQL.

choices.text: Returning a value is not allowed in Airflow 3
choices.why: Returning small values is how XComs work.

prompt: Why was `shop_nightly` paused when it first appeared in `airflow dags list`?
hint: Think of a file copied in by mistake.

choices.text: Every new DAG starts paused
choices.why: Right. Nothing runs on its own until somebody unpauses it.

choices.text: It had an error
choices.why: An error would stop it loading; it loaded fine.

choices.text: Its start date was in the past, so the scheduler refused it
choices.why: A past start date is normal.

choices.text: `dags test` pauses DAGs while it runs them
choices.why: It was paused before any test ran.

prompt: How many lines did one `airflow dags test` run of `shop_nightly` print before the filter?
hint: The second command of the first run.

prompt: In the first test run, `transform` failed. Which tasks never ran?
hint: Everything after a failed task waits for it.

choices.text: `extract` and `day_to_load`
choices.why: Both ran and succeeded before `transform`.

choices.text: Only `fact_sales`
choices.why: The dimension loads also wait for `transform`.

choices.text: The three loads after it
choices.why: Right. Each waits, directly or not, for `transform`.

choices.text: All six, because the run failed
choices.why: Two had already succeeded.

hint: Look at how the value ends.

choices.text: `run_sql.sh` was not executable
choices.why: It is run with `sh`, and it never got that far.

choices.text: A value ending in `.sh` is read as a template file name
choices.why: Right. Airflow looked for a file called `sh run_sql.sh` in the DAG folder.

choices.text: The `cwd` was wrong
choices.why: The working directory is used only once the command runs.

choices.text: Jinja does not allow spaces
choices.why: The fix is in fact a space.

prompt: Why does the lesson prefer `BashOperator`s that call Ana's own scripts over operators that do the work inside Airflow?
hint: Where else can the same work be run?

choices.text: `BashOperator` is faster than every other operator
choices.why: Speed is not the argument.

choices.text: Other operators need a paid licence
choices.why: Providers are open source.

choices.text: Airflow 3 removed the SQL operators
choices.why: `SQLExecuteQueryOperator` is there.

choices.text: The same command reruns by hand
choices.why: Right. Terminal, `nightly.sh` and Airflow all run it the same way.

prompt: Airflow reads a connection from an environment variable named `AIRFLOW_CONN_` followed by the connection's id in capitals, so the connection `wh` is `AIRFLOW_CONN____`.
`fact_sales` has arrows from `day_to_load` and from `dim_customer`. When does it start?

choices.text: When either one succeeds
choices.why: By default a task waits for all of its upstream tasks.

choices.text: When both have succeeded
choices.why: Right. All upstream tasks, by default.

choices.text: At 02:00, whatever their state
choices.why: The schedule starts the run; arrows start the tasks.

choices.text: After `dim_book`, because it is written before it in the file
choices.why: The file's order means nothing; there is no arrow from `dim_book`.

prompt: A colleague adds a task `report` that reads `marts.fact_sales`, and forgets to give it an arrow from `fact_sales`. What happens?

choices.text: Airflow refuses to load the DAG
choices.why: That is what a cycle does; a missing arrow is valid.

choices.text: `report` waits for every other task
choices.why: A task with no arrows waits for nothing.

choices.text: `report` is skipped
choices.why: It runs, which is the problem.

choices.text: `report` reads whatever is there, and succeeds
choices.why: Right. Nothing fails; the report is quietly a day old.

prompt: Order these `shop_nightly` tasks so that each comes after every task it waits for.
The run with logical date 02:00 on 3 March starts six months late, in September. Which day does `day_to_load` return?
hint: It asks the run, not the clock.

choices.text: A day in September
choices.why: That is what asking the clock would give.

choices.text: 3 March
choices.why: It subtracts one day from the logical date.

choices.text: 2 March
choices.why: Right. The same day, whenever the run happens.

choices.text: Nothing: a late run is cancelled
choices.why: Late runs run; that is what makes reprocessing possible.

prompt: In Airflow 2, a daily DAG's run labelled 2 March executed early on 3 March. What does a plain `schedule="0 2 * * *"` mean by default in Airflow 3?

choices.text: A run at 02:00 whose logical date is 02:00 the same day
choices.why: Right. No interval behind it; the DAG decides what it loads.

choices.text: A run labelled with the previous day, as in Airflow 2
choices.why: That needs a schedule declared with intervals.

choices.text: A run every two hours
choices.why: `0 2 * * *` is minute 0 of hour 2, daily.

choices.text: A run at 02:00 UTC
choices.why: The DAG's start date is in São Paulo time, and so is the schedule.

prompt: `dim_book` and `dim_customer` have no arrow between them. What is different about how they run under `dags test` and under the scheduler?

choices.text: Nothing; both run them at the same time
choices.why: `dags test` runs tasks one after another in the terminal.

choices.text: One after another, then together
choices.why: Right. Which is why a missing arrow can pass a test.

choices.text: The scheduler runs them in alphabetical order
choices.why: Without an arrow, no order is promised.

choices.text: `dags test` skips tasks with no downstream
choices.why: `dim_book` ran in the test.

prompt: Which command runs a single task of a DAG, without its upstream tasks, to try a change?

choices.text: `airflow dags test DAG DATE`
choices.why: That runs every task.

choices.text: `airflow tasks test DAG TASK DATE`
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: `airflow dags unpause DAG`
choices.why: That lets the scheduler start runs; it runs nothing now.

choices.text: `airflow dags reserialize`
choices.why: That reads the DAG folder again; it runs no task.

choices.text: A small value the next task needs
choices.why: Right. A date, a file name, a count.

choices.text: Moving a day's orders between tasks
choices.why: Data moves through the warehouse, not through Airflow's database.

choices.text: Storing the DAG's code
choices.why: The DAG processor stores DAGs; XComs are values from tasks.

choices.text: Sending a message to the person on call
choices.why: That is lesson 10's alerts.

prompt: The shop's database committed 14 transactions in two quiet minutes while `by_shop.py` sat in the DAG folder, one of them the query that measured it. At that rate, about how many transactions a day would the never-run DAG cause? Give a whole number.
hint: Thirteen per two minutes, times the two-minute periods in a day.

prompt: Where does the lesson say a DAG whose shape depends on data should read that data?
hint: Declare at the top; fetch at run time.

choices.text: At the top of the DAG file, cached in a global
choices.why: The top of the file runs on every parse, cache or not.

choices.text: In the scheduler's configuration
choices.why: Configuration holds settings, not data.

choices.text: In an environment variable set by the lab
choices.why: That fixes the shape when the lab is built, not when data changes.

choices.text: Inside a task, mapped at run time
choices.why: Right. Dynamic task mapping exists for that.

prompt: A DAG passes `airflow dags test` every time, and under the scheduler it sometimes loads facts with the previous night's customers. What is the most likely cause?
hint: What runs in sequence in a test and in parallel under the scheduler?

choices.text: The scheduler uses UTC
choices.why: Time zones would shift days, not customers.

choices.text: A missing arrow from the customer load to the fact load
choices.why: Right. The test's sequence hid it; parallel runs expose it.

choices.text: XComs are lost between scheduled runs
choices.why: Each run keeps its own XComs.

choices.text: The DAG is paused
choices.why: A paused DAG would not run under the scheduler at all.
